newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia stocks end lower after late sharp slide.
newsitem.headline: Australia stocks end lower after late sharp slide.

text.p: Australian shares ended lower on Friday with investors still nervous before the weekend following the hawkish comments by U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan made earlier in the week.
The All Ordinaries index ended 14.8 points lower at 2,449.9 after falling nearly 30 points in a late afternoon flurry.
Brokers said arbitrage trading between the futures and physical market caused both markets to fall sharply in late trade, before investor buying steadied some pre-weekend nerves.

Rodney Green, chief investment officer at Perpetual Funds Management, said investors were getting a little nervous before the weekend, particularly as overseas markets are still digesting the Greenspan comments made on Wednesday.
"I think the Greenspan comments over the past couple of days has made people a little nervous. People are probably thinking they don't want to take the risk over the weekend," Green said.
"There is some arbitrage trading going on," he said.
"The futures have fallen away, as the discount was widening, so people were buying futures and selling physical," he said.
Base metals miner Pasminco Ltd, Rupert Murdoch's News Corp Ltd and building materials group Boral Ltd were the most actively traded amongst the majors.
A higher gold price and firmer base metal prices helped push up resource share prices. The gold index recorded the strongest move by any local sector and the media sector was the weakest.
Brambles Industries fuelled the corporate earnings charge on Friday with a 14.3 percent rise in first half net profit, but its shares remained steady at A$21.70.
Gold miner Acacia Resources and paper group Spicers Paper both reported lower profits while metal fabrication group G.E. Crane and fruit canning group SPC both reported higher profits.
The March share price index futures contract was 33 points down at 2,426, off its Friday low of 2,422, widening the discount to the underlying index to 27.9 points.
